idea: traceturn is deterministic forensics for multi-agent transcripts. It finds the agent that first stated each shared number, counts how many later statements were independent checks versus echoes, finds wrong numbers that spread before anyone corrected them, and links the acts agents took on a number (submitted, posted, wrote, handed off) back to whether anyone had reported checking it. No model reads the transcript, so every result re-derives offline and can be tamper-checked in the browser. Run on the AI Village chat and computer-use logs and the German Wiki incident export.

wedge.title: traceturn
wedge.sector: AI SAFETY · Autonomous Swarm Forensics, Causal Blame & Claim-Lineage Analysis
wedge.target_user: Incident investigator, AI safety researcher, or trust & security engineer auditing out-of-control multi-agent swarms under incident pressure
wedge.painful_moment: Facing 200,000 turns of multi-agent tool logs and message threads during a cascading agent runaway, collusion, or benchmark cheating incident with a post-mortem deadline measured in hours, not weeks — and no way to tell which bad action caused the damage versus how a single false premise convinced the whole group it was legitimate.
wedge.unusual_constraint: No model in the attribution path: the kernel is a pure function of the transcript, so every result re-derives offline.
wedge.proof_metric: Every verdict re-derives byte-identical offline from the transcript: `pnpm claim:verify` re-derives all report totals, every pinned manifest and every act manifest, and `/verify` re-runs the kernel in the browser. Accuracy is measured on hand-labelled held-out samples (docs/AUDIT.md, docs/ACT_AUDIT.md).
wedge.essential_sponsor_role: High-level semantic intent classification and intent-drift scoring on flagged DAG subtrees, with deterministic heuristic fallback when offline.

adversarial_critique.why_generic_risk: Judges may see another LLM log-summarizer; must prove the deterministic graph kernel detects causal dependencies, circular validation, and permission escalation that simple chat prompting completely misses. The Claim Lineage graph is the direct counter-proof: show the same incident as blame-DAG-only, LLM-summary-only, and DAG+lineage, and point at the collusion ring the first two miss.
adversarial_critique.obvious_competitor: Generic observability platforms (LangSmith, Arize Phoenix) that trace single-agent latency/tokens but lack swarm-level coordination topology, independent-derivation counting, and causal blame slicing. They also cannot count independent verification paths across 170k messages.
adversarial_critique.unprovable_claim_risk: Claiming 100% detection of all possible covert coordination; scope proof strictly to committed incident fixtures (AI Village, German Wiki, and synthetic collusion benchmarks) with an honest precision/recall matrix. Independent-derivation counts are a lower bound — absence of provenance edges is not proof of fabrication.
adversarial_critique.superficial_sponsor_risk: Using Anthropic API as an ungrounded summarizer rather than a targeted semantic verification step on deterministically isolated anomaly clusters. Graph construction must stay 100% deterministic and offline; the LLM may only classify already-isolated subtrees.
adversarial_critique.hour_8_kill_criterion: The core deterministic parser and DAG builder must execute end-to-end against real collusion.wiki / AI Village slices and correctly identify the ground-truth inflection turn with PASS/FAIL verdicts by hour 8. Claim Lineage is explicitly SECOND priority: build it only after the blame DAG passes its fixtures. A working single-graph tool beats a broken two-graph tool.

demand_signals.direct_quote: We don't have good approaches for understanding/overseeing the activity and aims of AI 'swarms' — Ryan Greenblatt, Hugging Face incident investigator.
demand_signals.notes: Direct event premise and hackathon problem statement.

demand_signals.direct_quote: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
demand_signals.notes: Featured kickoff lecture for the hackathon. Direct evidence for the Claim Lineage wedge: cheating propagated via a shared knowledge library (Appendix D, 'Agent Local Wikis') then peer-to-peer messages — an epistemic failure before a behavioral one. Independent-derivation counting over that library is exactly what a summarizer cannot do.
